title: Internal Jugular Vein & Thrombosis Protocol
trigger_patterns: Doppler ultrasound reveals stagnant or retrograde internal jugular flow (< 2 cm/s)
Elevated D-dimer biomarker or visible unilateral cervical venous distension
Selected by trained crew during operational Doppler surveillance

steps.text: Position crew member in standardized restraint and deploy vascular ultrasound probe to the left and right internal jugular veins.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Evaluate Doppler flow direction and cross-sectional compression. Flag stagnation, spontaneous contrast, or non-compressible thrombus.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Cross-check bedside biomarker cartridge for D-dimer elevation and record resting jugular venous pressure.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: If occlusive or non-occlusive filling defect is identified, initiate onboard mission medical kit review (enoxaparin subcutaneous vs apixaban oral supply).
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Log all anticoagulant doses, times, and inventory levels into the encrypted medical telemetry ledger.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Execute deceleration tapering checklist: plan anticoagulant cessation 72 hours before re-entry or aerobraking G-load to prevent deceleration trauma hemorrhage.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure

steps.text: Transmit standardized Doppler cine loops, cross-sectional diameter measurements, and clinical summary to ground flight surgeon.
steps.source: LIGHTMINUTE demonstration protocol - not an operational NASA medical procedure
